clinician.trajectory_summary: A 57-year-old postmenopausal woman presented with three months of right breast swelling, pain, and bloody nipple discharge. Physical exam showed diffuse thickening and erythema without palpable mass. Mammogram revealed a 7.5 cm retroareolar mass with skin and trabecular thickening. Ultrasound showed a hypervascular complex cystic mass with thick irregular walls and abnormal axillary lymph nodes. Initial skin punch biopsy showed only inflammatory changes. Incision and drainage of purulent fluid improved symptoms. An ultrasound-guided core biopsy was performed and revealed a benign intraductal papilloma. Surgical excision was ordered but pathology results were unavailable.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial presentation with right breast swelling, pain, bloody nipple discharge, and inflammatory breast exam findings
Mammogram and ultrasound demonstrated a suspicious 7.5 cm complex cystic mass with skin changes consistent with inflammatory and mass features
Skin punch biopsy showed inflammatory changes but no neoplasm
Incision and drainage yielded purulent fluid with clinical improvement
Ultrasound-guided core biopsy pathology revealed benign intraductal papilloma
